title: Metamorphosis is often, perhaps always, accompanied by loss of bulk and weight

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Metamorphosis is often, perhaps always, accompanied by loss of bulk and weight

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Negative growth, an actual loss of bulk and weight, often and perhaps always accompanies metamorphosis, as in the eel, the silkworm before pupation and the frog tadpole.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The negative growth, or actual loss of bulk and weight which often, and perhaps always, accompanies metamorphosis, is well shewn in the case of the eel.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter III, “The Rate of Growth”; topic “Growth epochs and metamorphosis”. Scope: animals with metamorphosis (insects, amphibians, eels)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch03-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The pre/post mass contrast is simple and highly discriminating. Public datasets can test representative species and readily challenge the universal extension, but taxonomically broad paired measurements require substantial compilation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure the same individuals' wet or dry mass immediately before and after metamorphosis across eels, insects and amphibians. Frequent mass loss supports often, while a well-sampled class showing stable or increased mass would refute always.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Hydration and gut evacuation can mimic tissue loss.

Often has no explicit frequency threshold.

Relevant measurements are scattered rather than standardized.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A loss of mass at metamorphosis is a simple before-after contrast, and published series for the eel, silkworm, and frog exist to be compiled. There is no open dataset designed for that contrast across metamorphic animals, so the universal suggestion cannot be closed, and water loss confounds tissue loss. The named cases are partly resolvable; the claim in full is not.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare live mass just before and just after metamorphosis in eels, insects such as the silkworm, and amphibian tadpoles. A net loss would support the claim for that species; a well-measured metamorphic group that does not lose mass would weaken the suggestion that the loss always occurs.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Weight series through metamorphosis are scattered across experimental papers.

Loss of water or gut contents can be recorded as loss of bulk without loss of tissue.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.8
data existence: 0.45
